The PLAYBOOK `optimize_product_2` (`services/agent/playbooks/optimize_product.py`): step 6 — the `update_product_price` CONFIRM step at `optimize_product.py:125` — is deleted, and `required_steps = ("update_product_listing", "update_product_price")` (`optimize_product.py:72`, inside `OPTIMIZE_PRODUCT_TERMINATION_POLICY`) collapses to the one-lever shape ADR-090 d.4 names: one confirmed write, or a terminal tool call. The CONCURRENCY FIELD-LOCK MAP `FIELD_SCOPE_BY_OPERATION` (`services/agent/runner/concurrency.py:180`) loses its `"update_product_price": ("price",)` entry, so `field_scope_for("update_product_price")` raises `UnknownConcurrencyScopedOperationError` — the map's own documented contract for a tool name it does not own. `"update_product_listing": ("title", "description", "images")` must be byte-identical after the diff.

The IMPACT READER'S MEASURABLE SET, and this is the surface most likely to be edited by mistake. `workers/impact_reader/queries.py::measurable_tool_names()` (`queries.py:41-65`) is DERIVED from `services/agent/composition.py::measurable_write_tool_names()` (`composition.py:163`) unioned with the frozen legacy literal `{"listing.optimize_product"}`. Deregistering the spec therefore removes the name from the measurable set AUTOMATICALLY, with zero edits to `queries.py` or `composition.py`. The scope-verification report's line that removal "also touches `impact_reader/queries.py`'s measurable-tool derivation" describes the CONSEQUENCE, not an edit site — hand-adding `update_product_price` to a literal to keep old rows scannable would re-create exactly the hand-maintained-literal defect #1219 fixed.

OPERATOR-VISIBLE consequence of that derivation, stated plainly because it is a real loss and not a no-op: `load_measurable_executions` and `load_touch_dates` both filter `ToolExecution.tool_name.in_(measurable_tool_names())` (`queries.py:118`, `:141`, `:253`). Any ALREADY-WRITTEN `update_product_price` execution whose T+7 or T+14 window has not yet been read stops being selected the moment this deploys — its pending reading is silently never taken. Existing `impact_readings` and `tool_executions` rows stay valid and readable; what is lost is the FUTURE read of an in-flight execution. Count those rows on the candidate before merge and record the number on the issue; do not describe this slice as "only new scans stop matching" without that count.

NO HTTP surface changes. Nothing under `backend/src/juli_backend/api/routes/` is opened, no `/v1/**` or `/demo/**` request or response model moves, no field is added or removed from any payload a seller or the demo app reads. Nothing under `apps/`, `packages/` or `ios/` is touched — those are on this epic's doNotLoad list.

INTERMEDIATE STATE, deliberate and stated: between this slice and #1778 the workflow has NO price lever at all. A run proposes one listing field or concludes. That is the correct intermediate — it is not a regression to be patched with a temporary fallback, and the seller-visible effect (no price proposal for the duration) is accepted by ADR-090 d.1.

Mixed-version hazard: `juli-api` and `juli-celery-worker` must both be restarted onto the same release. A stable worker still holding the old registry while the candidate API serves the new playbook could dispatch `update_product_price` for a run created under the new shape; the retained-stable rollback below assumes both processes move together.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing about the deployed system changes: `update_product_price` stays registered and dispatchable, step 6 stays in the playbook, `required_steps` keeps demanding two confirmed writes, `"price"` keeps its field-lock entry and the impact reader keeps scanning price executions. That is today's state — nothing is exposed, nothing is partially applied, no data hazard, and no seller sees a difference.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Code-only rollback: redeploy the previous release and restart `juli-api` AND `juli-celery-worker` together. There is no schema to revert and no downgrade to run — this slice owns no migration. Runs COMPLETED under the candidate stay valid: they recorded one confirmed write and a real stop reason, and the reverted code reads both unchanged. A run SUSPENDED at CONFIRM across the rollback resumes correctly, because consent is bound by `params_sha` over the tool call's arguments and neither the arguments nor the hash function move in this slice — assert this pre-merge rather than assuming it. The one asymmetry to state out loud: a `update_product_price` execution that fell out of the measurable scan during the candidate window becomes scannable again after the revert, but its T+7/T+14 window may have passed in the meantime, so the reading is not recovered by the revert. Restart both processes on the same release; a stable worker on the old registry beside a candidate API on the new playbook is the one mixed-version state this slice must not sit in.
